properties.description:
crates/reflow2-core/tests/an_approval_does_not_erase_authorship.rs — 11 tests, plus the updated an_acknowledgement_says_whose.rs, the MCP a_constructor_accepts_the_owners_word_in_one_call.rs helper, and two new cases in tools/test_check_intent_authority.py.

MERGE (fail when authored_by is reverted to replace): author then approve keeps both roles and both dates and drops the single-valued slot; the set is in canonical order whatever the write order; a legacy author edge survives a new approval.

SHAPE: the same role twice is one role with the latest date; no role means author; an unknown role is refused and nothing is written; normalising the set shape changes nothing; a stray legacy `role` beside a set is dropped, not merged.

MIGRATION: migrate_authored_by_roles rewrites legacy edges once and is idempotent; a legacy export is normalised on import.

READERS: an approver who also authored still counts as the approver in loop_status's assigned decisions; the intent-authority tool reads the set and still refuses a set with no approver.

THE ONE THAT EARNED ITS KEEP: "the same role twice is one role" failed on the first draft and exposed that the normaliser's legacy default was being applied to an empty map — a bug two sibling tests had passed over.
properties.name: Approving what you authored keeps both roles — eleven tests, falsified by reverting the merge to a replace
